name: Miguel Cardoso
scopeNote: Two counted spells: Esperance de Tunis (2024-01-12 to 2024-10-22; Tunisian Ligue 1 2023-24 title, CAF Champions League final lost to Al Ahly) and Mamelodi Sundowns (2024-12-10 to ongoing; 2024-25 Premiership, CAFCL 2025 final lost to Pyramids, CAFCL 2026 final vs AS FAR, MTN8 2026). Sources call the model 'ofensivo, dominante, equilibrado' (A Bola) with a 4-2-3-1 base morphing to 3-2-5 / 2-2-4-2 in possession; the popular 'defensive coach' label is a critics' narrative that Cardoso rejects. Tactical coverage of the Esperance spell is thin (Tunisian columns and his press conferences only); Sundowns coverage is mostly Mozzart Sport match analyses (tier B). Exact day dates: Esperance start 2024-01-12 and end 2024-10-22 from the brief (Africa Soccer dismissal article dated 2024-10-23); Sundowns start 2024-12-10 (club announcement). Marking scheme (zonal vs man) of his own teams not stated by any source found.
openQuestions: No source found stating whether his teams mark zonally or man-to-man in open play; only an offside trap in a 5-4-1 (Pirates, 2026) and 'slack marking' vs Pyramids (EWN) are documented.

Esperance 2023-24 formation and pressing are undocumented in tier A-B sources; Kapitalis columns (author says he is not a technician) describe a median-then-compact defensive block and counter-attacking approach, and call Cardoso too defensive, while Cardoso says Esperance dominated the final first leg.
Mozzart Sport (Kenya) analyses are tier B by choice (match-specific, named tactical author unknown); formations vary between pieces (4-2-3-1 base, 4-3-3 vs Al Ahly).
Kapitalis 2025-04-09 attributes the 'defensive' criticism at Esperance to lack of attacking recruits; contested by supporters' view in the same outlet.
Portuguese originals of quotes mostly unavailable: Sundowns press conferences are in English; Mosaique FM quote is French rendering.

statedView.quote: “In the beginning, people were saying, ‘Ah, maybe coach Miguel’s style is not exactly Sundowns’ style’. That’s absolutely wrong,” (Sundowns Pitchside Podcast; English rendering of spoken Portuguese-accented English)

“I was in Portugal for a long time, considered a coach who was too romantic in the way I think of the game. People like some more objectivity or direct game, or speed. They don’t like being under pressure in the build-up and still try to do it. And I was this kind of coach there.
“I want a team that can control the games. Controlling the games means the team must be solid in the four moments of the game.”
“Having control of the game also has to do with being aggressive in the moment you lose the ball”
“Despite people saying, you coach, you are defensive. That’s bullsh*t. So what I mean is, it’s not true, we wanted to bring that energy to win the match.

"Nous n'avons pas joué un jeu défensif au match aller ... Quand vous regardez la finale de l'Europa League entre le Bayer Leverkusen et l'Atalanta, il n'y avait pas de défense ni d'attaque, il y avait un équilibre et c'est ce que nous voulons" (French rendering of press conference; Portuguese original not found)
«Perceber o que foi feito, o que poderia ter sido melhor e o que ainda está por fazer.» / «ninguém chega aqui sozinho.»
“We are used to controlling matches in the South African league ... Now we must prepare mentally to adapt to situations where our opponents will have the majority of possession.”
“I’d like Sundowns to understand that [we need to rotate] ... managing the group is using the ones in better conditions to play.”
